insight: Home only appears after Firebase anonymous sign-in plus 3 sequential Firestore reads (profile, scores): LCP ~2.5 s even on localhost with a warm cache. Cold first paint (~3.3 s) is blocked by the render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet in index.html. Baseline: .gstack/benchmark-reports/baselines/baseline.json (main 7b3affd).

Right after npm installs a new bun.exe on this Windows PC, it can be locked (EBUSY: used by another process) for ~30 s, most likely an antivirus scan, so gstack tools that run on bun (qa deadline, evidence) fail. Wait until bun -e works before guarded probes, and never batch probe+checkpoint pairs.

On Windows Git Bash, the gstack-upgrade inline flow guard compares git rev-parse --show-toplevel (C:/Users/...) with pwd -P (/c/Users/...), so it always says not a gstack checkout. Compare with pwd -W instead; the rest of the flow works.

In browser tests, focusing #board from code after a mouse click does not match :focus-visible, so Board.svelte stays out of keyboard mode and the first Enter only reveals the cursor. Reach the board with Tab (as a keyboard user does) before pressing Enter.

baselines/baseline.json (2026-09-30) was measured with live Firebase, and a first visit writes users/{uid}. To compare a branch without touching production, build main in a scratch git worktree (link node_modules with node fs.symlinkSync(target, path, "junction"); mklink via Git Bash mangles /J), serve it on 4174 beside the branch on 4173, and measure both back to back with Firebase hosts blocked and Google Fonts allowed. Before removing the worktree, unlink the junction; TaskStop on vite preview leaves node.exe listening, so kill the PID on the port.

gstack setup on this Windows PC can stop with exit 126 because /usr/bin tools (sed, tr, basename) or bun.exe are briefly locked (Device or resource busy), likely antivirus during setup process storms. It leaves the previous install in place; retrying ./setup --host claude a few minutes later succeeded (2026-10-11, third try).

The test route regex that blocks googleapis.com also matches fonts.googleapis.com, so screenshots silently use fallback fonts instead of Unbounded and Manrope. Block Firebase with a hostname predicate that skips fonts.* hosts.

Online play is testable without production: build with vite build --mode emulator, serve it, run the Firebase emulators (npm run emulators), drive host and guest as two Playwright contexts, drop and restore a connection with window.__dnbNet.offline()/online() (emulator builds only), read the emulator DB via REST with header Authorization: Bearer owner, and load the published rules with PUT /.settings/rules.json?ns=demo-dnb-default-rtdb to prove a client works before new rules are published.

On Windows, stopping firebase-tools (TaskStop on emulators:start, or the end of emulators:exec) can leave the database and firestore emulator java.exe processes listening on 9000 and 8080. Before starting emulators or npm run test:rules again, end the PID listening on each port.

Patching scratch scripts by piping a node script through a quoted heredoc, with a JS template literal holding regexes or escaped quotes, repeatedly lost the backslashes (a digit class turned into a plain letter class; an escaped apostrophe ended a string). Make such edits with the Edit tool, which is literal, then run node --check. Avoid backslashes in gstack-learnings-log JSON too: it rejects them on this PC.

To edit an app localStorage while the app is not running (for example to age a saved timestamp before a restart test), open a same-origin static file in the context. The first stylesheet in index.html is Google Fonts on another origin, so pick the link whose href starts with location.origin.

Firebase Realtime Database get() does not fail when the database cannot be reached: it waits for the server indefinitely, so any loading state built on it needs its own time limit (the online rejoin uses 8 s, then a message and Try again). Test it by aborting 127.0.0.1:9000 with context.route plus context.routeWebSocket in the emulator build.

Production bundles always contain the Firebase SDKs own connectFirestoreEmulator and connectDatabaseEmulator code, on main too. To prove no app emulator code shipped, grep dist and the live assets for __dnbNet, 127.0.0.1 and demo-dnb instead.

To prove a new browser check catches a bug: git stash the fix, rebuild the emulator bundle into the same outDir while vite preview keeps serving it (no restart needed), run the suite and expect FAIL, then stash pop and rebuild.

CSS ::before/::after text (like a tick on aria-pressed buttons) becomes part of the accessible name in Chromium, so screen readers read it and exact getByRole name lookups miss. Use content:"x"/"" alt text (keep a plain content declaration first as a fallback) or draw it with a mask.

On main, the Google font files from fonts.gstatic.com never appear in performance.getEntriesByType(resource), so transfer totals miss ~76 KB. Count them from network events (Playwright requestfinished sizes or CDP Network.loadingFinished encodedDataLength).

Cold Home timings on main swing with the render-blocking Google Fonts CSS (0.2-3.2 s on the same day). Compare warm medians, or add a throttled phone-like pass (CDP Network.emulateNetworkConditions + Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate) for a fair first-visit comparison.

getComputedStyle returns color-mix() results as color(srgb r g b) with channels from 0 to 1, not rgb(). Contrast scripts that pull the numbers out as 0-255 read them as near-black and report bogus ratios (20:1 on hover, 1.2:1 for text). Scale by 255 when the value starts with color(srgb.

The impeccable DOM scan cannot see gradient backgrounds or aria-hidden decoration: Neon by day brand text (on the slate band painted by a body gradient) shows as 1.0:1, and the decorative initials avatars as low-contrast text. Confirm by the element position against the gradient stops and by aria-hidden before counting them.

In browser tests, navigating away from the game screen (goto or reload) saves the game on screen over any dnb:active you just seeded and reopens it. Leave through the app first (Home button, accept the confirm), then seed dnb:active and load Home.

Board surfaces with a light-from-above gradient are far lighter than their token where play happens: Tabletop at night felt token #2F3F39 renders about rgb(96,110,105) under the light, so a turquoise focus ring measured 5.3:1 from tokens but 2.5:1 from pixels. Check indicators on textured or lit surfaces against screenshot pixels, not tokens.

gstack-qa-deadline 900 s counts wall-clock, including writing each checkpoint with the full exact observed text (about a minute for a 90-line output). Write new probe scripts before starting the deadline, order probes by risk, print details only on failures, and run the remaining suites as separate PR checks.

To measure text contrast over textures: wrap each visible text node in a span with visibility:hidden (layout unchanged, hides colour emoji and shadows too), screenshot, then per-pixel contrast of the text colour (alpha-blended) against the pixels under each Range client rect, 5th percentile; skip rects whose elementFromPoint is an overlay; restore the nodes. Script: texture-text.mjs in the session scratchpad.

When Claude Code stops a background vite preview shell for low memory, the node child keeps listening on the port and serving dist/; it even served a fresh build with new hashed file names without a restart (2026-10-13). Check the port (netstat, curl) before assuming the server is gone.

The design detector DOM dump inlines the whole stylesheet, so rules for themes that are not active (Neon glows, Tabletop plank stripes, Neon grid) produce one row per page in every theme. Judge dark-glow, stripes and grid rows per active theme from screenshots, and compare rule counts only across runs on the same page set.

A CSS background-image texture on a large element (the board felt) becomes the LCP element, and inside the screens 0.32 s entrance fade its LCP is recorded when the fade ends (about 480 ms vs 140 ms with Animations off). Before calling an LCP jump a regression, list the LCP entries with their elements, with Animations on and off.

When memory is tight (Claude Code reaps idle background shells), serve main and branch builds from one foreground node process for the duration of each measurement: scratchpad serve-two.mjs <branchDist> <mainDist> -- <command>, which exports BRANCH_URL and MAIN_URL to the child. Same server code for both keeps the comparison fair.

An SVG filter (feGaussianBlur, feOffset merges) on a single horizontal or vertical <line> uses its zero-height (or zero-width) bounding box, so the filtered line draws nothing. Put filters on groups whose bounding box is 2D (like g.lines) or leave single straight lines unfiltered.

Playwright has no touch drag; use a CDP session: Input.dispatchTouchEvent touchStart, several touchMove, touchEnd (touchPoints [] to lift). With touch-action:none on the target, Chromium delivers pointerdown/move/up with pointerType touch, so drag gestures can be tested headless.

Perf probes that dispatch synthetic PointerEvents must also count, per step, whether the element being timed is on screen; otherwise they can time nothing. In dots-boxes, main press preview is an unclassed dotted line (svg > line[stroke-dasharray]) while the branch drag line is line.drag, so a class-only selector reported 0 on main.

On this Windows PC, cold FCP or ready medians from 2 cold loads swing by +-25 ms (+30%) in both directions between identical builds. Before calling a warning, re-run the flagged scenario with 4-6 cold loads (and 30+ warm). Every first-pass flag in the drag benchmark went flat that way.

Sound QA that only records OscillatorNode.start frequencies misses the real failure: an AudioContext made before user activation starts suspended, so notes start while paused (late or lost). Record ctx.state at every oscillator start and tap the output with an AnalyserNode to measure the level; run Chromium with --autoplay-policy=document-user-activation-required so it behaves like Chrome.

The owner browser Brave can be driven headless by gstack playwright-core with executablePath C:/Program Files/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/Application/brave.exe (throwaway profile, Brave defaults). Never run brave.exe --version on Windows: it opens a real Brave window and the command hangs.

Inside gstack-qa-deadline, run long suites as sh -c with the suite output redirected to probe-NNN-full.txt and a summarize step that prints only counts and FAIL lines; checkpoints then quote a few lines exactly instead of 90-108.

In dots-boxes the audio engine starts only on real user activation, so move-to-paint probes that dispatch synthetic PointerEvents never run the sound path. Time Sound-on moves with page.mouse.click / page.touchscreen.tap (perf-sound.mjs: window capture pointerup to two rAFs) and count notes started while the context is running.

To test spring or elastic motion in a browser, record the element geometry every requestAnimationFrame (path d parsed to tip and curve midpoint) and assert overshoot, settle frame and rest stability (unchanged d after 300 ms means no frames left running), plus the Animations-off path. dots-boxes spring-test.mjs does this for the drag band.

For thin decorative strokes (landing rings, dashed guides), measure contrast from pixels: hide the element, capture, sample the board along its path and compare with its computed stroke colour (median and 10th percentile). Token contrast misses lit or textured surfaces; dots-boxes ring-contrast.mjs does this.

dots-boxes perf probes (drag-perf, perf-filters) set anim false in saved settings, which skips any motion feature (springs, turning rings). Benchmark motion with anim true (drag-anim-perf.mjs: moves, 1.5 s held-still frame intervals, let-go intervals) and expect about one slow frame per 360 on both builds as noise.

In pixel label-contrast probes, read getComputedStyle values (color, size) into plain variables BEFORE hiding the text with an inline transparent colour: CSSStyleDeclaration is live, so reading cs.color afterwards returns rgba(0,0,0,0) and every ratio is measured against black (fake 1.5:1 on dark buttons, fake passes on light ones). Also color-mix() results compute to color(srgb r g b) with 0-1 channels.

The /qa browser Full clock (900 s wall clock, checkpoint writing included) fits about 12 one-suite probes of this repo (about 610 s of command time); order them by risk and put the unchanged-code suites (integrity, resume) last. Translucent tokens (Neon glass board rgba) break token-based contrast math in probes: measure those boards from pixels.

impeccable DOM mode inlines the whole stylesheet, so rules scoped to another theme (Neon hover glow #21bdca, Neon board grid) are reported on Tabletop and Paper pages too; check the selector applies to the page before counting a hit. In this repo dark-glow, cramped-padding (turn pill track), codex-grid and repeating-stripes are by-design repeats; avatar initials are decorative low-contrast hits deferred to the spec step 3.

rAF frame intervals and main-thread metrics cannot see compositor or GPU cost (a CSS transform animation under backdrop-filter glass showed 16.7 ms frames while the GPU process burned 38-70% of a core). Measure GPU process CPU time with a browser CDP session: SystemInfo.getProcessInfo cpuTime deltas over a few seconds, main vs branch. Drag perf at 12x12 1920x1080 exposes per-frame backdrop-filter re-blur when the filtered element changes underneath.

Since step 2, Paper draws board lines as path.ln curves (M x1 y1 Q qx qy x2 y2) with a .ln.ghost twin each on boards up to 6x6, straight <line> elsewhere. Probes that select .lines line or count .ln miss or double-count them: read ends from either tag and use .ln:not(.ghost). Landing rings also have a circle.land.land-core twin (shown only in Neon at night): count rings with :not(.land-core).

Per-theme suites that open each theme in a fresh context never exercise a theme switch with moves on the board; Board takes the skin as a prop, so add a mid-game switch probe (top bar picker, radio by name, Esc) whenever board drawing depends on the skin.

Firebase RTDB get() on a path with an active onValue listener returns the cached server value without a round trip (repoGetValue checks syncTreeGetServerValue first), so it cannot detect a dead connection or fetch missed updates. To prove liveness, get() a path nobody listens to (e.g. this player own presence node) and race it against a timeout; on timeout goOffline()+goOnline() forces a fresh connection and resync.

Chrome CDP network throttling does not delay WebSocket frames, so it cannot simulate mobile latency for Firebase. Put a Node TCP proxy between the browsers and the database emulator (emulator on 9002 from a temp firebase.json, proxy on 9000 where the emulator build connects) that delays each chunk in order; to simulate a silently dead connection, drop one connection data both ways while its sockets stay open. Scratchpad delay-proxy.mjs, online-freeze.mjs. On Windows emulators:exec leaves Java on 8080/9000/9002: kill listeners before each run.

bench-palettes.mjs always measures main then branch per scenario. When one scenario keeps differing, rerun it with serve-two.mjs given the two dists swapped (branch dist in the main slot): if the gap follows the build it is real, if it follows the slot it is order bias. Paper at night Home showed +45 ms cold for the branch in both slots on 2026-10-15 with only 1.3 KB of start-up JS different: under the 20% warning line, recorded as noise.

AI property tests on random positions must stay outside Hard exact-search window (5x5: more than 32 of 60 lines left): inside it perfect play may legally sacrifice 3+ boxes while a safe line exists. Replay failures with the exact search (exactBest via a patched copy exposing _dbg) before calling them bugs.

To time AI replies in the browser, log every line count change with performance.now() in the page (MutationObserver) and attribute lines to the AI unless they followed the human tap; time from the previous line, not until it is the human turn again (extra turns after boxes chain several AI moves). Scratchpad ai-browser.mjs.

ai.ts used to import ai-core.js statically for its no-worker fallback, which put the whole AI engine in the page start-up script; making the fallback a dynamic import (loaded only when the worker fails) cut the entry by 8.7 KB gzip. Watch the entry chunk whenever ai-core.js grows.

Chromium still downloads the background-image of a ::before/::after whose content is none (the pseudo-element is never drawn). When a mode drops a pseudo-element that another mode gives a texture, also set background:none, or the hidden texture is fetched (Tabletop at night fetched the day rim wood, 45 KB, until fixed). Check with a request log, not screenshots.

To prove a theme has no violet, measure screenshots in 4x4-pixel block averages (hue 255-300, saturation >= 0.18): per-pixel counts pick up text anti-aliasing fringes (about 0.02-0.06% on dark brown pages) that are not real colour. Overlapping translucent light mixes too: magenta or pink light over navy or over blue/cyan light turns violet, so keep Neon rooms neutral and pick player colours whose glows do not mix to violet (blue + teal, not blue + raspberry). Scratchpad violet-check.mjs.

On this Windows PC a Playwright chromium.launch can fail with spawn EBUSY right after another browser run (the headless shell executable is briefly locked, most likely by antivirus). It is an environment failure, not a product result: record the probe as not run and replay the same command a few seconds later (it passed on the retry).

tests/theme/theme-colours.test.ts (npx vitest run tests/theme) checks that every mode s browser bar, picker preview and index.html pre-paint colour equal the --page its own app.css block sets. Run it after any palette change: the bar map in themes.ts and the inline map in index.html are easy to forget (Dark Neon kept a stale bar until QA).

When Windows background work (svchost servicing, indexer, sync) keeps the CPU 75-87% busy, plain main-then-branch benchmark medians contradict themselves run to run. Interleave builds load by load (order flipping each round, 15 rounds) and read the paired difference (scratchpad reload-ab.mjs); check the CPU load first with Get-Counter Processor(_Total). With under 1 GB free, Claude Code reaps background benchmark shells: run heavy ones only when memory allows.

SVG layers hidden with display:none via CSS tokens are still created and laid out by Svelte: the themes branch board built Neon glow, reflection and tile shapes in every mode and appeared 8-14% later on a game reload. Build theme-only layers behind {#if} on app.settings.skin/theme (Board.svelte, HeroBoard.svelte) and keep the tokens for how they look.

To show a coloured texture tile (the day maple wood, the day paper) in another colour without a new asset, multiply the tile onto base = target * 255 / tile_mean per channel: the result averages the target exactly (Tabletop/Paper at night: wood over #B77D5F and paper over #A75E2F average Sienna #A0592B). Measure text over the lightest texture pixels (base * tile max), from pixels: the design detector reads the base colour (it cannot see blend modes) and reports false low-contrast rows.

A textured mid-tone page (Sienna #A0592B, luminance 0.15) leaves no room for warm off-white small text: #F5EEE6 measured 4.0-4.4:1 over the light grain, only #FFFFFF keeps 4.5:1 (4.6+). Text straight on such a page needs the page ink (--head-text) and on-page rules for .tag, .hero .kicker and help/muted text outside cards; cards keep --text.

texture-text.mjs used to measure screen-reader-only text (.sr, 1px clipped; e.g. the game announcement) and Paper s brand underline (.brand .mark-paper touches the text box bottom), both reading as false contrast failures; it now skips .sr and hides the underline while sampling. Check its FAIL lines for these before calling a contrast bug.

To prove a Web Worker stops (e.g. Hard pondering on Quit), sum renderer cpuTime from a browser CDP session (SystemInfo.getProcessInfo); it includes worker threads (1017 ms/s during a 0.7 s playout). Pick a moment the worker is surely busy: on 4x4, pondering at 28 lines left finishes in a fraction of a second, so quit at 30-31 left (968 ms/s before, ~140 after on Home).

Browser probes that play whole games must bound the loop by player turns plus a wall-clock cap, not by loop iterations: waiting iterations (20 ms polls while the AI thinks) exhausted a 400-iteration guard on a Hard 5x5 game at 55 of 60 lines. Give each probe its own screenshot names so reruns never overwrite earlier evidence.

Under CDP CPU throttling (4x) a Web Worker that starts computing at page load (Hard pondering on a resumed game) delays the main thread: the board appeared 12-26 ms later on a late-game reload, level on an early-game reload with nothing to ponder. Isolate such findings by varying the state (moves drawn) rather than adding rounds; defer start-up worker work past the first paint.

A board marker drawn in the dots colour at about the dots size (Tabletop last-move pip: 0.085 vs 0.075 of a gap) reads as one more board dot; the mockup set its pip apart by colour. Rings in the dot or mover colour did not stand out on a 7x7 either. Prototype marker candidates by restyling the live SVG element in the page (no rebuild) and compare whole boards, not only close-ups.
Scratchpad dr-marks.mjs joins its output paths without a slash (OUT + name): pass both dirs with a trailing slash, or the shots and DOM dumps land one level up with the dir name glued to each file.

Scratchpad suites carry expectations patched for designs that later changed (patch-probes-pencil.mjs taught spring-test and marks-test that all of Paper draws pencil); after a design change, a suite failure on exactly the changed rule is usually a stale fixture: confirm against the agreed design and the old patch before calling a product bug. board-contrast.mjs reads only <line> elements, so curves (Paper pencil) go unmeasured; use line-contrast2.mjs.

When interleaved wall-clock reloads swing (the same build measured 518 and 592 ms in two runs), read Chrome own counters per reload (CDP Performance.getMetrics: ScriptDuration, RecalcStyleDuration, LayoutDuration, TaskDuration) to split JS from rendering cost; reload-metrics.mjs does it. A 2-round frames run flagging a few points of long frames needs a 4-round rerun before calling it.

An SVG filter with the default objectBoundingBox region on a group paints NOTHING while the group geometry box has zero height or width: a lone line, or lines all along one row or column. The board group .lines took Tabletop/Paper filters, so each game first line(s) stayed invisible until a line in the other direction arrived (owner saw it as lag, a broken Random starter and hover-drawing). Use filterUnits=userSpaceOnUse with the whole board as the region. Probes that read styles or the DOM cannot see it: check pixels (paint-check.mjs, paint-collinear.mjs).

The Bash tool cwd resets to the parent folder (C:/Users/10xosborn/SWE/Grid Rivals), where gstack-slug resolves to GridRivals instead of 10xosborn-dots-boxes; cd into grid-rivals in the same command before gstack-slug, gstack-paths project dirs, review-log or learnings-log.

firebase emulators:exec runs its script through cmd on Windows, so Git Bash /c/Users/... paths get mangled; pass C:/Users/... paths in the script string and run it from grid-rivals (firebase.json: Database 9000, Auth 9099, Firestore 8080). Scratchpad online-fix.mjs (host desktop drag, guest phone tap, pixels and sounds on both screens) is the quick online check; run kill-emu.sh after.

To price SVG filter changes on the board, time taps from a FRESH game (empty board) rather than a crowded one: early-game is where a filter region sized to the drawn lines differs from a whole-board one. Scratchpad filter-cost-ab.mjs (taps to paint, grow-frame intervals, renderer CPU per tap via SystemInfo.getProcessInfo; 4x4 phone CPU 4x and 12x12 desktop) measured the userSpaceOnUse switch at +2.5-5% renderer CPU on 12x12 and nothing on 4x4, frames unchanged.

On this PC jq is missing (the skill's approved.json and rerun snippets use it: do them with node), and gstack-taste-update writes to ~/.gstack/projects/grid-rivals/ (cwd basename) instead of the gstack-slug project 10xosborn-dots-boxes: move taste-profile.json there after it runs. For theme work, real CSS prototypes injected with page.addStyleTag over a build (scratchpad glass-proto.mjs, glass/glass-<V>.css) plus the compare board on screenshots beat AI mockups: they measure for contrast (board-contrast.mjs and line-contrast2.mjs take CSS_FILE) and GPU (glass-gpu.mjs).

gstack 1.91.171 design-detect refuses targets outside the repo or the design-report folder (DETECT_REFUSED, then DETECT_NO_TARGETS, exit 0): copy dumps into designs/design-audit-*/dom/<run>/ and pass a C:/ path (a /c/ path also printed nothing); its JSON goes to stdout. A design-shotgun compare --serve leaves a design.exe daemon running that locks design/dist/design.exe, so gstack setup fails with EPERM: stop the daemon (netstat for its port) before upgrading.

To prove a decorative layer never paints over a dialog, comparing screenshots with the layer shown and hidden fails on frosted (translucent, backdrop-blurred) panels and rounded corners, which show the page by design. Paint the dialog solid green and the suspect layers solid magenta (thick), sample inside the corners, and require zero magenta (scratchpad glass-explore.mjs CASE=dialogs).

Decorative layers drawn OVER animated SVG content (a masked ::before rim and a full-size ::after of gradients at z-index 2) get re-rastered wherever the content repaints: on Neon by day it cost ~30% more renderer CPU per tap on a 12x12 board (headless software raster) while frames and tap-to-paint stayed the same. Measure such layers with filter-cost-ab.mjs on a big board; promoting them to their own compositing layer is the likely fix.

Drawing an SVG stroke in with pathLength=1 and stroke-dasharray:1: the hidden state (offset 1) leaves a dash ending exactly at the path start or end, and with round caps that shows as a dot. Hide it with the dash wholly off the path (dasharray 1 1.5, offset 1.25). vector-effect:non-scaling-stroke with preserveAspectRatio=none breaks pathLength dashes in Chromium (part of the line shows when hidden, part missing when shown).

An underline absolutely positioned under an inline Kalam name vanished: Kalam content box is taller than its line box, so the line sat outside the overflow:hidden name row and was clipped. Make the name a flex item that truncates itself and holds the underline in its own padding (align-items:baseline keeps the note beside it aligned).

Svelte 5 drops spaces at the start and end of an element: a span holding space-dot-space rendered as Your turn.+1 with no gaps, and a span holding Your turn. plus a trailing space ran into the next sentence. Put the spacing in CSS margins or write the text as a template expression in braces. Flex containers also eat edge spaces of anonymous text items, so keep sentence text in a block, not a flex row.

An underline absolutely positioned under an inline Kalam name vanished: the font content box is taller than its line box, so the line sat outside the overflow-hidden name row and was clipped. Make the name a flex item that truncates itself and holds the underline in its own padding; align-items baseline keeps the note beside it aligned.

With body overflow-x hidden, a horizontal-overflow check on documentElement.scrollWidth passes even when the page is too wide: in mobile emulation an element wider than the screen widens the layout viewport itself (innerWidth reported 370 or 398 on a 360 px phone). Check innerWidth against the viewport width you set.

Scratchpad integrity-r1a I5b and qa-r1a A2, A4 and A5 read the board right after a reload into the AI turn and race the AI 250-450 ms pause (since PR 20): they fail on main and on branches alike when the machine is busy (I5b 3 of 3 on a base build). Replay, or hold the AI with a silent Worker stub before reading, before calling it a regression.

A nowrap child of a column flexbox with align-items flex-start keeps its whole text width even when every parent has min-width 0, so it spills out of a shrinking chip. Cap it with max-width min(9em, 100%) so its ellipsis follows the box.

Home-load FCP on this app swung +200 ms between builds over 8 interleaved rounds (phone CPU 4x) with LCP and ready flat, and vanished at 15 rounds; game reloads showed a +359 ms paired median at 10 rounds that became -61 ms at 15. Run 15 rounds before calling a load regression.

Realtime Database rules can do the arithmetic for game checks: % and / give exact integer division, a number joined to an empty string is a child key (child((x + 1) + )), and a number only equals a $path variable after the same join. A generator (scripts/database-rules.mjs) inlines the expressions; a 6 KB move check runs fine on the emulator.
gstack-qa-deadline run refused a command whose emulators:exec script string held escaped quotes (Deadline guard failed); put the command in a small sh wrapper and run the wrapper under the guard.

container-type (size or inline-size) applies layout containment, which makes the element the containing block for position:fixed descendants. A size container wrapping a fixed overlay (the game ResultsModal, a toast) would pin it to the container instead of the viewport. Keep size containers (.play, .hero) off any ancestor of fixed overlays; on the game screens the modal is a sibling of the .game section, outside .play.

To compare a TS layout module (boardFit.ts) with the real page, strip its types with Node 24 module.stripTypeScriptTypes, inline its one import, gather its exports on window and addInitScript it into the page; Vite 8 uses Rolldown, so esbuild is not in node_modules. step4/fit-check.mjs in the scratchpad: 420 boards, predicted and measured dot gaps equal.

A browser probe that counts lines after the player taps must read within about 150 ms: the AI answers 250-450 ms later (PR #20), so a 400-500 ms wait sees two new lines and an exact +1 check fails although the tap worked.

Layout maths that predicts another screen (boardFit for the size picker) must measure the screen with visualViewport.width x scale (capped by innerWidth), not innerWidth/innerHeight alone: a page that overflows on a phone (Setup custom steppers at 320-360 px) widens the layout viewport (360x640 read as 373x664) and the picker offered boards with dots under 40 px. tests/layout/boardFit.regression-1.test.ts stubs window/visualViewport/document in node to cover it.

Since step 4 the offline notice (Firebase blocked in every probe) floats over the game screen top bar until dismissed. A probe that clicks the game top bar (theme button, brand, chip) after a reload into a game must click Dismiss first, or Playwright reports that the .banner intercepts pointer events (theme-switch.mjs fixed this way).

When transparent UI (Paper spread score sheet and board) sits over a textured, blended background drawn by pseudo-elements, every change re-rasters the texture under it: +10-13% renderer CPU per line on 12x12. Giving the background pseudo-elements their own layer (will-change: transform) cut it to -27/-31% vs the old sheet. Measure with filter-cost-ab.mjs and CSS_BRANCH injection before editing source.

On this PC under memory pressure, per-build medians of tap-to-paint swing +4% to +41% between identical runs while the round-paired differences stay within a few ms; trust paired differences and CDP counters (Performance.getMetrics, renderer cpuTime) and rerun before bisecting, or the bisect chases noise (step 4: a CSS bisect gave opposite answers in two runs).

A native <dialog> with its own padding: a click on that padding has event.target === the dialog, exactly like a backdrop click, so an onclick backdrop-close handler also closes it when the user taps empty space inside the card. Give the dialog padding 0 and wrap the content in a body element that fills it (ThemeSheet already did; ConfirmDialog needed .cf-body).

A canvas sized only by its width/height attributes (innerWidth*devicePixelRatio) displays at that bitmap size in CSS px: confetti.ts drew 780x1688 on a 390 px 2x phone with the burst at the right edge. Give it CSS width and height 100% (position fixed inset 0 does not stretch a replaced element).

A native modal dialog makes the page inert but Tab from its last control still leaves to the browser chrome (headless shows activeElement = body). The spec asks for a focus trap: src/lib/focus.ts wrapTab on the dialog keydown wraps first<->last, counting only tabIndex >= 0 controls (roving radios skipped). Probe: step5/tab-wrap.mjs.

The .dc.html mockups need a support.js that is not in docs/design/mockups, so they cannot render whole; their dialog <section> is static inline-styled HTML, so step5/mockup-dialogs.mjs renders just that (with the helmet styles) at 390x844 for side-by-sides (fonts may fall back to serif offline: compare layout, not type).

Probes written for the browser confirm() (page.on(dialog, accept)) read state on the line after the click; the themed confirm (a dialog.confirm answered asynchronously) breaks those reads, not the product. Step-5 suite copies inject an init script that clicks the dialog action button when dialog.confirm[open] appears, and qa-r1a B6 waits for the Continue card to detach before reading.
